## Setting
Dividing the utility bills. The five people in a shared house have been splitting gas, water, and electricity in a way that was agreed when only three of them lived there. - The last twelve utility statements
- Monthly settle observed at another house

- Sunlight and heating need by room
- Payment log for the last twelve months
- Settling up when the last rooms filled

On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. ## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|

## Your profile
Name: Mio
Age: 17
Gender: female
Personality: Mio has a cheerful and energetic personality that naturally makes those around her smile. She is curious and loves to try new things. She can be a little clumsy at times, but people tend to laugh it off and forgive her when she makes mistakes. She has strong opinions of her own, but is also able to listen to the opinions of others, making her a well-balanced person.
Concern: I have started doing arithmetic in my head before switching anything on, and last winter I sat here in a coat rather than be the one who turned the heating up. What we choose will quietly decide how this place feels to live in, and I would rather that were said aloud than discovered in February.

## Plan
The discussion follows this plan.
- Round 1: The group discusses the need for a new system and what data is required to make a fair choice. They focus on cost, administrative effort, and historical usage patterns.
- Round 2: Participants share the findings from their research. They debate the trade-off between precision in billing and the emotional or administrative cost of achieving that precision.
- Round 3: The group evaluates the three proposed options against their discovered constraints. They weigh the benefits of predictability, fairness, and simplicity before voting.

Each participant's part:
- Mio: Cares about the psychological comfort of the living environment. She looks for a way to use utilities without anxiety.

## Setting
Dividing the utility bills. The five people in a shared house have been splitting gas, water, and electricity in a way that was agreed when only three of them lived there. They are deciding how the bills will be divided from now on. Participants: Ryuji, Rin, Mio, Shunichi and Misaki. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Electrician's quote for the rooms
- The last twelve utility statements
- Monthly settle observed at another house
- Trial run of a reconciliation template
- Kitchen notice about the cooler
- Winter habits at a house paying ahead
- Plug-in monitor readings room by room
- Sunlight and heating need by room
- Payment log for the last twelve months
- Settling up when the last rooms filled

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Mio, Ryuji, Rin, Shunichi and Misaki. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the options | 4 turns | every participant votes; the option with the most votes is adopted |
- Several participants may choose the same thing; what is found out is told only to the participant who looked into it.
If votes are tied, one of the tied options is chosen by a fixed rule. The discussion ends after the vote.

## Looking into things
After round 1, each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into. What they find out is told only to that participant.

## Your profile
Name: Misaki
Age: 24
Gender: female
Personality: Misaki has a calm personality and tends to deal with things in a cool-headed manner. She may seem a little unfriendly at times, but she is actually very kind at heart and does not hesitate to lend a helping hand to those in need. She does not express her emotions outwardly and does not talk much about her relationships with those around her, but she is often relied upon by those close to her. She can be a little absent-minded at times, but her quiet demeanor is one of her charms.
Concern: Money has started to sour how we speak to each other here: a reminder gets read as an accusation, and whoever sends it is avoided for a week afterwards. I would rather look squarely at where the bills have already damaged things between us than keep smoothing it over.

## Plan
The discussion follows this plan.
- Round 1: The group discusses the need for a new system and what data is required to make a fair choice. They focus on cost, administrative effort, and historical usage patterns.
- Round 2: Participants share the findings from their research. They debate the trade-off between precision in billing and the emotional or administrative cost of achieving that precision.
- Round 3: The group evaluates the three proposed options against their discovered constraints. They weigh the benefits of predictability, fairness, and simplicity before voting.

Each participant's part:
- Misaki: Aims to eliminate interpersonal conflict and social tension. She weighs options based on their potential to reduce friction between housemates.

Vote request. Output only the label of one option.
Candidates: A, B, C
